text:
maya: quick q — i'm exploring splitting the onboarding validation pipeline into a lightweight fast-check on ingest vs a deeper offline bench. want to nail interface boundaries and rerun semantics before i write the rfc. open to bikeshedding now?
jordan: +1. what are you picturing as the fast-check surface area? smoke for correctness + tiny perf profile?
maya: exactly. fast-check should be ~30s and gate obvious regressions: model loads, forward pass sanity, basic outputs for golden prompts, kv-cache sanity on short seqs. deep bench runs larger evals, perf curves, quantization sims.
kevin: we should define an explicit contract between them. fast-check returns a small JSON summary with status + short fingerprints. deep-bench consumes that fingerprint to avoid re-running trivial steps.
sasha: important: compatibility checks need to include runtime-specific invariants (e.g., allocator failures, broadcast dims, attention mask quirks). fast-check can be permissive but must catch fatal incompatibility.
maya: agree. thinking: fast-check status: PASS / WARN / FAIL. WARN triggers an automated retry (n=1) and a quick triage job; FAIL blocks staging. deep-bench can be scheduled async and report metrics to console.
devon: how do we prevent combinatorial explosion with multi-weights/quantizations? deep-bench should be able to take a "profile set" and run variants in parallel on dedicated bench fleet. fast-check only validates a canonical flavor.
jordan: +1 to canonical flavor. if we accept a quantized artifact, fast-check should still attempt a lightweight decode to ensure op-compat. but heavy quantized perf stays in deep-bench.
kevin: operators: where does this run? fast-check on the intake worker (short-lived pod) vs deep-bench as a batch job on GPU pool. need failure-budget rules.
maya: proposal: fast-check: cpu/gpu light pod (nodeSelector: onboard-fast), timeout 45s. deep-bench: k8s job with resourceProfile: bench-large. put both configs in model entry descriptor. snippet:```yaml
onboard:
  fast_check:
    timeout: 45s
    node_selector: onboard-fast
  deep_bench:
    schedule: async
    resources: bench-large
    variants: [fp32, int8]
```
sasha: love the descriptor approach — makes rollbacks easier. also we should include a "skip_deep_bench_if" predicate (e.g., small model < 1B, or fast-check PASS+low-variance).
devon: telemetry: fast-check should emit compact telemetry: load_time_ms, mem_peak_mb, simple_quality_score. deep-bench emits full eval sets and histograms. UIs/alerts rely on those keys.
jordan: also record commit/build ids + environment (cuda/cudnn versions) so we can triage infra-induced deltas.
kevin: edgecase: what if fast-check passes but deep-bench finds perf regression. rollback flow? automatic pin to previous model and notify owner + create incident?
maya: prefer automated soft-fallback: route live traffic to previous variant, mark the model as quarantined, and create ticket with deep-bench artifact attached. ops-bot: can we auto-create the ticket and attach deep-bench link?
ops-bot: yes — we can wire the bench runner to call /incidents/create with payload {model, bench_link, summary}. i've got a small PR ready for the webhook.
sasha: question on golden prompts: who owns the golden set? per-team or central? golden drift leads to noise.
devon: recommend two-tier golden: shared canonical for infra checks + team-specific sets for quality. deep-bench runs both.
maya: ok action items: (1) i'll draft RFC for pipeline descriptor + PASS/WARN/FAIL semantics, (2) kevin/jordan to propose retry/fallback policy and failure budgets, (3) sasha/devon to write telemetry keys and golden set ownership proposal, (4) kevin to hook ops-bot ticket flow. aim to have draft in 1 week.
jordan: sounds good. adding: include a small conformance test harness (python) that fast-check runs to normalize outputs across runtimes.
kevin: lgtm. i'll spin up a quick PoC — small container that runs the YAML descriptor and emits summary JSON.
maya: thanks all. i'll post the RFC draft tomorrow morning and drop links here. :thumbsup:
